messages:
Alex: quick follow-up on the private endpoint fallback idea. sketched an alternate flow using short-lived, signed relay tokens + regional SNAT pools. want feedback on TTL, revocation, and operational signals. cc @Maria @Kevin

Maria: sounds promising. prefer short TTLs and avoid a global revocation DB if possible. short list + GC for edge cases.

Kevin: SRE concerns: token issuance spikes during connector restarts and how we map tokens to ENI/NATs. need rate limits and metrics. what happens if issuance fails? fail open to global egress or fail closed?

Alex: thinking failover to a global egress pool (higher-cost, lower-priority) with telemetry and customer notification so apps stay up.

Jordan: implementation note: don't allocate an ENI per token. pool ENIs and keep ephemeral token->5-tuple SNAT mappings pinned for token duration. re-use IPs while keeping attribution.

Chris: security: tokens must bind to connector identity + audience + nonce and be KMS-signed. two revocation models: (1) very short TTL (5m) so revocation is rare; (2) short TTL + revocation list for abuse. require mTLS for connectors.

Alex: proposal sketch: POST /v1/relays/token authenticated by connector bootstrap -> returns { token, expires_at, assigned_pool } Token payload fields: connector_id, pool_id, nonce, iat, exp signed by CP KMS. default TTL = 5m, account-configurable with guardrails.

Maria: if TTL=5m, add clock-skew tolerance and a refresh endpoint so connectors can prefetch; log a token_use counter for debugging.

Kevin: ops playbook: rate-limit per-account (e.g., 100/min), emit metrics (token_issued, token_failed, pool_exhaustion), alert on sustained issuance spikes.

Jordan: mapping behavior: pool_id -> IP set; mapping table with TTL=token.exp; reclaim mappings on expiry; eviction policy for long-lived sticky sessions vs churn. keep mapping table in-memory in the regional relay plane and persist snapshots for crash recovery (avoid single DB hot path).

Chris: audit: append issuance events to CP audit stream immediately. tokens must include audience claim (e.g., outbound:egress) to prevent reuse across flows. never log raw tokens (only token_id).

Alex: two open questions: default TTL 5m vs 15m? and support for long-lived bootstrap tokens for offline connectors?

Maria: default 5m. bootstrap tokens allowed as one-time long-lived seeds that exchange for ephemeral tokens when online; require strict rate limits and audit.

Kevin: agree 5m. bootstrap tokens issuance should be an admin action with MFA and revocation hooks. also monitor token churn per account to detect automation loops.

Jordan: region-local in-memory mapping table with snapshotting sounds best. avoid central sync on the hot path.

Chris: ensure token encryption-in-flight and at-rest; redact tokens in logs; keep token_id->audit mapping.

relay-bot: Token service rollout started in staging region-3 at 2026-03-23T15:22:04Z :rocket:

Alex: thanks everyone. action items: i'll update the RFC with a flow diagram, default TTL=5m, bootstrap-token model, and a small spike to measure SNAT/ENI scaling. please add blocking concerns as comments on the RFC. i'll post the update tomorrow. :thumbsup:
